replies.author: Rainstruck
replies.body: I'm going to have to agree with what zoom said. He is correct when stating that new players won't really know some of the commands and that we should proceed to say, "Don't publicly accuse others of hacking, please use /report." The reason that this works well is because it will allow new players to learn how to report players that may or may not hack. The reason that this doesn't work is, like many have stated before, they will find other ways of saying: hacks, hacker, and hack. Its just like some other sayings. Take eZ for example, it is a way to say, "Easy" without typing as much. So they can say hak instead of other spellings. So for this I would say +1, -1. In the short run it seems like a good idea but in the long run it doesn't seem like it would have a good effect in the long run.

replies.author: Matic0B
replies.body:
This won't solve anything.

Some people might use the word hack in a way that doesn't break rules. Example below.
Player A: What is forcefield?
Player B: It's a hack. Don't use it or you can get banned.
That doesn't break the rules but helps player A with his question and tells him that its illegal to use it.

And like any other filter it could easily be bypassed. They get stopped once and then start bypassing the filter making it useless. Putting a space or a dot in there would bypass it (unless it would could stuff like that in).

Since it would be so easy to bypass theres no point working on it. It will be a waste of time. And we have all these amazing staff members to take care of rule breakers so we don't need a filter.

replies.body:
maybe if this gets implemented, also block slurs. fag, faggot, the n word, etc. swear words are usually fine for people and a good way to vent in the chat as long as they're not directed towards others, but slurs can be more damaging even when they're not directed at others. and just try to filter out any combination, if it's worked on hard enough (which it won't be i'm sure) you can get most combinations of "hax", "hacker", etc.
also, i've been punished before for joking and saying "hax!!!11!" when it was clear the person was just good at pvp and we were joking around. i just brushed it off because it doesn't matter; i know that i didn't do anything wrong. and yes, after a certain number of infractions you can get banned, but honestly just don't break the rules and that won't happen...
